title: PhonePe Revives IPO Plans, Eyes March 2027 Listing At Up To $15 Bn Valuation
summary: Walmart-backed PhonePe revives IPO plans targeting a March 2027 listing at up to 15 billion dollars
detailed: PhonePe revived its IPO plans, targeting a March 2027 listing at a valuation of $12 billion to $15 billion.
The company plans to file updated IPO papers for an offer for sale of up to ₹12,000 Cr ($1.3 Bn), following a $14.5 Bn valuation in a 2025 secondary investment.
Walmart-backed fintech PhonePe and investment bankers are involved in the listing discussions.
The revival follows a previous pause due to market volatility and depends on regulatory clarity regarding UPI merchant discount rates and market-share caps.
sentences: Walmart-backed fintech major PhonePe has revived its IPO plans and restarted discussions with investment bankers, targeting a March 2027 listing at a valuation of $12 Bn to $15 Bn, sources told Inc42.
The Bengaluru-based company plans to file updated IPO papers by December-end for an offer for sale of up to ₹12,000 Cr ($1.3 Bn).
Notably, PhonePe was valued at $14.5 Bn during General Atlantic’s $600 Mn secondary investment in 2025.

Sources said PhonePe expects greater clarity by December-end on two regulatory issues affecting the company’s business – the merchant discount rate (MDR) framework for UPI transactions and the 30% market-share cap for third-party UPI apps.
A possible extension or relaxation of the cap could ease a regulatory overhang ahead of the proposed listing, the sources said.
PhonePe declined to comment on the IPO development.
The Economic Times first reported on the revival of its listing plans.
The renewed push comes after PhonePe paused its IPO plans in March, citing geopolitical uncertainty and volatility in global capital markets.
At the time, the company said it would restart the process once markets stabilised.
The rally in Indian equities and foreign portfolio investors’ return to net buying appear to have given PhonePe greater confidence to revive its listing plans.
PhonePe is seeing stronger growth in lending and operating revenue, the sources said.
The company’s lending business has grown around 100%, while operating revenue has increased 35%-40% QoQ.
The company is also expected to report a net profit, they added.
This would mark a turnaround from FY26, when PhonePe reported a net loss of ₹2,792 Cr.
Operating revenue rose 11.5% to ₹7,920.5 Cr from ₹7,105 Cr in FY25.
The lending business offers PhonePe a route to diversify revenue beyond its core payments operations.
Its growth and contribution to profitability will be relevant to the company’s pitch to public market investors.
Beyond financial performance, the regulatory outlook remains central to PhonePe’s IPO preparations.
Introducing MDR on select UPI transactions could create an additional revenue stream for payment companies.
However, whether such charges will be introduced remains uncertain.
The other issue is the National Payments Corporation of India’s (NPCI) 30% cap on UPI transaction volumes handled by individual third-party application providers (TPAPs).
NPCI had extended the compliance deadline for existing apps exceeding the cap to December 31, 2026.
PhonePe operates above the threshold, making any further extension or relaxation significant for its growth plans ahead of the proposed public market debut.
Its renewed listing push also coincides with IPO preparations at payments infrastructure major Razorpay.
Razorpay has received SEBI’s approval for its proposed ₹5,000 Cr–₹6,000 Cr public offering.
It is targeting a valuation of around $5 Bn (₹47,000 Cr), with a listing likely between January and March 2027, sources previously told Inc42.
The timeline could put its debut ahead of PhonePe’s proposed March listing.
